title: WorldPop population 2025, 1 km (R2025A, constrained, UN-adjusted)
description: Estimated people per 1 km pixel, constrained to built-up areas and adjusted to UN national totals.

title: Global Power Plant Database v1.3.0
description: Power plants with capacity, fuel and location, as of 2021. Used only to fill the capacity (and name) of a plant OpenStreetMap maps without one, from the same-fuel plant within 3 km.
vintage: WRI Global Power Plant Database v1.3.0 (2021), capacity fill only

title: OurAirports airports
description: Airport locations, IATA codes and types.

title: GeoNames gazetteer, Vietnam
description: Place names and coordinates of Vietnam's cities and towns.

title: IBTrACS v04r01, Western Pacific
description: Best-track positions of every tropical cyclone in the Western Pacific basin, 3-hourly.

title: OpenStreetMap rivers of Vietnam
description: Every river relation in Vietnam that carries a Wikidata link (the notable rivers), with its geometry. Drawn as map art in place of Natural Earth's sparser lines inside Vietnam; width follows length.

title: OpenStreetMap military land of Vietnam
description: Areas mapped as military land (landuse=military or a military=* tag: airfields, naval bases, barracks, training areas, ranges), with their outlines. Vietnam publishes no list of installations; OSM shows what mappers have drawn, so coverage is uneven and most sites have no name.

title: OpenStreetMap power plants of Vietnam
description: Every feature mapped as a power plant (power=plant) in Vietnam, with its source (plant:source), capacity (plant:output:electricity) and name. Coverage depends on mappers: most large plants and many solar and wind farms are mapped, but some lack a capacity tag and rooftop solar is not mapped as plants.

title: OpenStreetMap port areas of Vietnam
description: Port land, harbours and port terminals mapped in Vietnam (landuse=port, industrial=port, harbour=*, seamark:type=harbour), and features named Cảng… or Bến cảng…, with their centres; used to position the listed seaports.

title: OpenStreetMap expressways and national roads of Vietnam
description: Every way mapped as highway=motorway (expressways, cao tốc) or highway=trunk (national roads, quốc lộ) in Vietnam, with its route number (ref) and geometry. Slip roads (motorway_link) are left out.

title: OpenStreetMap railways of Vietnam
description: Every way mapped as railway=rail in Vietnam (service tracks such as sidings and yards excluded), with its usage tag and geometry.

title: OpenStreetMap national parks of Vietnam
description: Areas mapped as national parks in Vietnam (boundary=national_park, or protected areas of IUCN class 2), with their centres; used to place a park that Wikidata has no coordinates for.

title: Quyết định 804/QĐ-TTg: Danh mục cảng biển Việt Nam (8 July 2022)
publisher: Prime Minister of Vietnam (Thủ tướng Chính phủ)
description: The official list of Vietnam's 34 seaports (cảng biển) with their class under Decree 76/2021/NĐ-CP: 2 special, 11 class I, 7 class II, 14 class III. The signed scan is transcribed in the pipeline; the port areas used to place each seaport follow the seaport master plan (Quyết định 1579/QĐ-TTg, 2021).

title: Danh sách vườn quốc gia tại Việt Nam
description: The list of Vietnam's national parks with year of establishment, area (ha) and province. Each park is created by a decision of the Government or the Prime Minister; Wikipedia compiles the list, it is not itself an official register.
vintage: Vietnamese Wikipedia, list of national parks (Nov 2026)

title: Đại học (Việt Nam)
description: The article on Vietnam's multi-campus universities (đại học): it names the national universities and the regional universities (đại học vùng). The Law on Higher Education defines the type but names no university; each is set up by a Government or Prime Minister decision.
used_for: Wonders: which national and regional universities

title: List of the busiest airports in Vietnam
publisher: Wikipedia (figures from Airports Corporation of Vietnam, ACV)
description: Yearly passengers per airport, as compiled on Wikipedia from ACV reports.

title: Wikidata
description: Coordinates and facts for World Heritage sites, national parks, universities, ports, airports (Vietnamese names), landmarks and the islands of Hoàng Sa and Trường Sa, by SPARQL query.
used_for: Hoàng Sa and Trường Sa islands
Special national relic positions (where the relic's article has no coordinates)

title: Open-Meteo weather forecast API (current conditions)
description: Current temperature, precipitation, cloud cover, weather code and 10 m wind for 57 fixed grid points over Vietnam, fetched by the visitor's browser only when the Live weather layer is switched on (one batched request, cached 30 minutes). Weather data by Open-Meteo.com.

title: Resolutions on province-level boundaries, 1975–2008
publisher: National Assembly of Vietnam; texts from Wikisource (vi) and from thuvienphapluat.vn and vbpl.vn (Ministry of Justice) via the Internet Archive
license: Public domain (legal documents are not protected by copyright in Vietnam)
description: The National Assembly resolutions that merged, split or moved provinces: 27 Dec 1975 (northern mergers), 15 Jan 1977 (Côn Đảo), 29 Dec 1978 (Hà Nội, Cao Lạng, Duyên Hải), 30 May 1979 (Vũng Tàu – Côn Đảo), 28 Dec 1982 (Trường Sa), 30 Jun 1989, 12 Aug 1991, 26 Dec 1991, 6 Nov 1996, 22/2003/QH11 and 15/2008/QH12. Each lists the districts of the provinces it creates.

title: Vietnamese Wikipedia: province-level units year by year
description: The history section of “Đơn vị hành chính cấp tỉnh (Việt Nam)” (the number of province-level units at the end of each year and the changes behind it, with references), “Phân cấp hành chính Việt Nam” (the 1975–1976 mergers), and the pages of Hà Đông, Hà Sơn Bình, Mê Linh, Minh Hải and Cửu Long for the district moves the resolutions above do not spell out. Each file is one revision.

title: Viet Nam - Subnational Administrative Boundaries (COD-AB, 2020-10-27 release)
publisher: OCHA / Humanitarian Data Exchange; sourced from the Government of Viet Nam, vetted by ITOS (USAID). Copy retrieved from the Internet Archive (snapshot of 26 August 2022), as HDX no longer serves it
description: The 63 provinces and centrally-run cities before 1 July 2025 (admin level 1, vnm_admbnda_adm1_gov_20201027). Used for the inner borders between former provinces inside each 2025 province; the outer outlines come from the 2025 release.

title: Vietnamese Provinces Database v5.2.0: wards GIS (GeoJSON)
publisher: Thang Le Quoc (GitHub), from the Vietnam Administrative Units Reference Map (sapnhap.bando.com.vn, Vietnam Natural Resources, Environment and Cartography Publishing House) and the NSO/GSO unit codes
description: Boundaries, names, kinds and official codes of the 34 provinces and 3,321 communes, wards and special zones of the two-tier local government that took effect on 1 July 2025, as updated to Resolution 388/NQ-UBTVQH16 (September 2026: twelve Bắc Ninh communes became wards; the count of units is unchanged). Geometry derived from the official reference map at sapnhap.bando.com.vn.

title: Viet Nam - Subnational Administrative Boundaries (COD-AB, v02)
description: The 34 provinces of 2025 (admin level 1, valid from 2025-09-25), sourced from the Government of Viet Nam: the map's province outlines, coast and land/water mask. It has no commune level.
vintage: COD-AB admin 1, valid from 25 September 2025 (34 provinces)

title: Ủy ban Thường vụ Quốc hội quyết định cả nước còn 3.321 xã, phường, đặc khu
publisher: VTC News (16 June 2025), summarising the 34 resolutions of the National Assembly Standing Committee
license: © VTC News; only the published counts (facts) are used
description: The official number of communes, wards and special zones of each of the 34 provinces as decided in June 2025 (3,321 = 2,621 communes + 687 wards + 13 special zones); used to check the boundary file.

title: Danh mục đơn vị hành chính Việt Nam (commune-level units)
publisher: National Statistics Office of Viet Nam (Cục Thống kê), danhmuchanhchinh.nso.gov.vn
license: Official state register; no licence stated, used with attribution
description: The official register of administrative units: code, name, type (xã, phường, đặc khu) and province of every commune-level unit, queried for the list in force on 28 November 2026 and on 1 July 2025. Both lists have 3,321 units; between them 22 communes became wards (10 in Đồng Nai, 12 in Bắc Ninh) and nothing else changed. Every unit's type and code on the map is checked against it.

files.note: SOAP 1.1 POST, action http://tempuri.org/DanhMucPhuongXa, DenNgay=28/11/2026 (the list in force on that date)
SOAP 1.1 POST, action http://tempuri.org/DanhMucPhuongXa, DenNgay=01/07/2025 (the list in force on that date)

title: Resolutions 237/NQ-UBTVQH16 and 388/NQ-UBTVQH16 establishing wards
publisher: National Assembly Standing Committee; texts as published by the Government portal (chinhphu.vn), the National Assembly's newspaper (Đại biểu Nhân dân, via VNA), VTC News and Thương hiệu & Công luận (the Bắc Ninh announcement ceremony)
license: Official state documents, cited with attribution; only the facts are used
description: Resolution 237/NQ-UBTVQH16 (adopted 14 April 2026, in force 30 April 2026) made 10 Đồng Nai communes wards; Resolution 388/NQ-UBTVQH16 (of 4 August 2026, in force 20 September 2026) made 12 Bắc Ninh communes wards, each on its former commune's area and population. The names they list are checked against the units whose type changed in the NSO register.

title: Bản đồ tra cứu các đơn vị hành chính Việt Nam: diện tích và dân số 2025 cấp xã
publisher: Ministry of Agriculture and Environment / Vietnam Natural Resources, Environment and Cartography Publishing House (sapnhap.bando.com.vn; ISBN 978-632-622-303-3)
license: Non-commercial public-service publication of the State ("xuất bản phẩm không kinh doanh, phục vụ cộng đồng"); used with attribution; only the facts are used
description: For each commune, ward and special zone of the two-tier local government: natural area (km²), population 2025 (people) and the resolution that formed it, as the official merger map's data service returned them on 28 November 2026; and the map's table of the 34 provinces with their 2025 population. Each value is checked against the unit's outline and WorldPop before it is shown (communes.json stats.rules).
vintage: Bản đồ sáp nhập (bando.com.vn), lấy ngày 28/11/2026; dân số 2025

title: Statistical Yearbooks of Vietnam 2019-2025 (full editions)
publisher: National Statistics Office of Vietnam (NSO, formerly GSO)
license: No licence stated; official statistics, reused with attribution
description: Full yearbooks 2019 to 2025 (bilingual). Their by-province tables give the years the 2025 yearbook no longer prints for the 63 former provinces (2019 and 2021; HDI 2019-2023; FDI and income per person 2019-2023, one year per edition). Each year comes from the newest edition that prints it, and an edition is used only if it agrees with the 2025 yearbook on the years both print. Parsed by pipeline/nso/backfill.py into data/stats/series/; each row cites its edition and page.

title: CHELSA V2.1 bioclimatic variables, 1981–2010 (30 arc-seconds)
publisher: WSL Swiss Federal Research Institute (Karger et al.)
description: Climate normals averaged over 1981–2010, downscaled from the ERA5 reanalysis with terrain-based models (Karger, D.N. et al. 2017, Scientific Data 4: 170122; data: Karger et al. 2021, EnviDat, doi:10.16904/envidat.228.v2.1). BIO1 annual mean temperature, BIO5 max temperature of the warmest month, BIO6 min temperature of the coldest month and BIO12 annual precipitation, read at 30 arc-seconds (~0.9 km) for the map window only.

title: Global Forest Change 2000–2025 v1.13
description: Landsat-based tree canopy cover in 2000 and the year of stand-replacing loss 2001–2025, 1 arc-second (~30 m) tiles 30N_100E, 20N_100E and 10N_100E, read every 4th pixel (~110 m) over Vietnam's mainland. Hansen, M.C. et al. 2013, Science 342: 850–853. A relative indicator of trends: the producers warn that sensors and methods changed over time and that pixel counts are not definitive area estimates.

title: Vietnamese Wikipedia: seasonal sights (Mù Cang Chải, Hà Giang, Mộc Châu, Điện Biên, Quảng trường Lâm Viên)
description: Month ranges of seasonal sights, each quoted word for word from the article's text: the terraced fields of Mù Cang Chải (water season May–June, ripe rice September–October) and Hoàng Su Phì (planting April–June, ripe rice August to mid-October), Mộc Châu's seasons (white mustard flowers November–January, plum and peach blossom January–March, bauhinia in April, ripe plums in May), the Điện Biên bauhinia festival (mid-March) and the wild sunflowers of Đà Lạt (late November). Places: the coordinates of the articles about those districts.
used_for: Season calendar: flowers and terraced fields

title: Wikidata: Quảng trường Lâm Viên (Q56072444) coordinates
description: The coordinates (P625) of Lâm Viên Square in Đà Lạt, where the wild-sunflower entry is placed.
used_for: Season calendar: place of the Đà Lạt wild sunflowers

title: Wikimedia Commons photos (place cards)
license: Each file's own free licence (CC0, public domain, CC BY, CC BY-SA)
description: The photos in a place card are fetched by the browser when the card opens (MediaWiki API: the place's Wikidata image, P18, when it has one; files found by the place's name near it; geotagged files nearest the point). Only files whose licence is CC0, public domain, CC BY or CC BY-SA are shown, each with its author, licence and a link to its file page; maps, logos, flags and diagrams are skipped by their file names. Nothing is stored by the atlas.

title: Airlines and destinations of Vietnam's airports
description: The "Airlines and destinations" ("Hãng hàng không và điểm đến") tables of the English and Vietnamese Wikipedia articles on the 22 Vietnamese airports with scheduled service, current revision (its id and timestamp are kept). Each row names an airline and the airports it flies to from that airport, with seasonal and charter services marked. Wikipedia editors compile the tables from airline announcements; they are not an official schedule and can lag behind or run ahead of what is flown.
used_for: Air routes (domestic, which airlines fly them)
vintage: Current revisions, 28 November 2026 (ids and timestamps in air_routes.json)

title: Digital elevation model of the Vietnamese Mekong delta (Topo DEM)
publisher: Minderhoud, Coumou, Erkens, Middelkoop & Stouthamer (2019), via PANGAEA
description: Elevation of the Vietnamese part of the Mekong delta, interpolated (empirical Bayesian kriging) from almost 20,000 elevation points of a 2014 national topographical map (1:200,000), in metres above the Hòn Dấu datum (mean sea level at the Hòn Dấu tide gauge); rivers and bedrock outcrops above +10 m are cut out. Published with Minderhoud et al. 2019, "Mekong delta much lower than previously assumed in sea-level rise impact assessments", Nature Communications 10:3847 (doi:10.1038/s41467-019-11602-1), which finds a mean elevation of about 0.8 m above sea level instead of the earlier assumed about 2.6 m.
used_for: Sea-level exposure in the Mekong delta (sealevel.json)

title: OpenStreetMap physical and economic geography of Vietnam
description: Named peaks and volcanoes (natural=peak/volcano, with ele), mountain passes (mountain_pass=yes nodes and the roads they lie on; named natural=saddle; roads named Đèo …), named lakes and reservoirs (natural=water with water=lake/reservoir/lagoon, landuse=reservoir) with their outlines, named dams (waterway=dam), border crossings (barrier=border_control), industrial parks (landuse=industrial named Khu công nghiệp / KCN / Industrial Park) with their outlines, and features named as craft villages (Làng nghề, Làng gốm, Làng lụa …). Coverage depends on volunteer mappers.

title: Wikidata battles fought in Vietnam, and river lengths
description: Items that are battles (instance of a subclass of battle, Q178561) with a coordinate in the box around mainland Vietnam, with their date, Vietnamese and English labels, Vietnamese Wikipedia title and number of Wikipedia sitelinks (used as the notability threshold); and the length (P2043) and basin area (P2053) of the rivers' Wikidata items, normalised to metres and square metres.

title: Lễ hội Việt Nam (danh sách một số lễ hội)
description: The table "Danh sách một số lễ hội" of the Vietnamese Wikipedia article on Vietnamese festivals: start day in the lunar calendar, place and festival. Positions come from the article linked in the festival cell (its GeoData coordinates, or its Wikidata item's P625), else from the most specific place linked in the place cell. Wikipedia compiles the table; it is not an official register and lists only some festivals.

title: Southeast Asia crop calendar: Vietnam rice
publisher: USDA Foreign Agricultural Service, International Production Assessment Division (IPAD)
description: Planting, mid-season and harvest months of Vietnam's rice seasons (North: winter–spring, main season; South: winter–spring, summer–autumn early and late) with each season's share of production. The chart was read against its month gridlines (the page has no table); the live host no longer resolves, so the Wayback Machine copy was used.
used_for: Living map: rice paddies by month

title: GIEWS country brief: Viet Nam (26 February 2026)
publisher: FAO Global Information and Early Warning System
description: FAO's crop calendar for Viet Nam's rice seasons, used as a cross-check of the USDA calendar.
used_for: Living map: rice paddies by month (cross-check)

title: Lũ ở Đồng bằng sông Cửu Long (Phạm Thị Huyền Trang & Trương Văn Tuấn)
publisher: Tạp chí Khoa học Trường ĐHSP TP. Hồ Chí Minh 3(81), 2016
description: The annually flooded upper Mekong Delta: '1.632.000 ha thuộc 8 tỉnh: Đồng Tháp, An Giang, Long An, Kiên Giang, Cần Thơ, Tiền Giang và một phần của Vĩnh Long, Bến Tre', and the season: inflow July–August, peak in September or early October at Tân Châu / Châu Đốc, recession from October to the end of December.

title: Flood forecasting in the Mekong (FAO document ac146e03)
description: 'every flood season from July to November' in the Mekong Delta: corroborates the season's months.

title: Nghị định 26/2019/NĐ-CP (Luật Thủy sản implementing decree), Articles 42–43
license: Vietnamese legal text (not subject to copyright)
description: Fishing zones: vùng ven bờ (coastal; around islands to 6 nautical miles), vùng lộng (inshore) and vùng khơi (offshore, to the outer limit of the EEZ), and which boats fish in each. The zone lines' coordinates are not in the decree body, so the boat lights are generic.

title: Âm lịch Việt Nam (Vietnamese lunar calendar tables and rules)
license: Free for personal, non-commercial use (the dates themselves are facts)
description: The year codes (TK20, TK21) of his amlich JavaScript, computed for 105°E (UTC+7): Tết = 1 January + the code's offset. His notes give the years Vietnam's Tết differs from China's (2007: 17 vs 18 February; 2030: 2 vs 3 February). Wayback copy (the live site returns 404).
used_for: Living map: Tết fireworks (Tết eve dates)

title: Gregorian–Lunar Calendar Conversion Tables
description: The Chinese calendar (UTC+8) for 1990–2040, a cross-check of the Vietnamese Tết dates.

title: GHS-BUILT-S R2023A: built-up surface 1975–2020 (1 km, Mollweide)
publisher: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (JRC), Global Human Settlement Layer
description: Built-up surface (m² of buildings per 1 km cell) from Landsat and Sentinel-2, observed epochs 1975–2020 every 5 years, 1000 km tiles R7_C28, R7_C29, R7_C30, R8_C29, R8_C30, R9_C30 of the Mollweide (ESRI:54009) grid. Pesaresi, M. and Politis, P. 2023, GHS-BUILT-S R2023A, JRC, doi:10.2905/9F06F36F-4B11-47EC-ABB0-4F8B7B1D72EA. The 2025 and 2030 layers of the release are projections and are not used.
used_for: Living map: cities grow with the year

title: Wikidata: opening dates of Vietnam's expressways (P1619)
description: The Wikidata items linked from OpenStreetMap's expressway ways (their wikidata tags), fetched with the wbgetentities API, plus a SPARQL list of every Vietnamese road, bridge and tunnel item with a date of official opening (P1619), matched to OSM ways without a wikidata tag by exact Vietnamese name. Only P1619 is used as an opening year; inception (P571) and start time (P580) are not.
used_for: Living map: expressways by opening year

title: Vietnamese Wikipedia: articles on Vietnam's expressways
description: Plain-text extracts (MediaWiki API) of the Vietnamese Wikipedia articles on the expressways named in OpenStreetMap. A reviewed table in the living-roads builder takes the year each named route or section opened to traffic (thông xe / khánh thành / đưa vào khai thác) from a quoted sentence of the article.
used_for: Living map: expressways by opening year

title: OpenStreetMap everyday places of Vietnam
description: Features mapped in Vietnam as hospitals (amenity=hospital), universities and colleges (amenity=university/college), schools (amenity=school), markets (amenity=marketplace), places of worship (amenity=place_of_worship, with religion=*), named historic features (historic=*), named beaches (natural=beach) and urban rail (railway=subway/light_rail and their route relations), with their centres and tags. Coverage depends on mappers: cities are mapped far better than the countryside, and many features have no name.

title: OpenStreetMap major road bridges of Vietnam
description: Road ways tagged bridge=* on expressways, national roads and primary roads (highway=motorway/trunk/primary and their links) that carry a name, with their geometry; the map keeps bridges 500 m or longer.

title: OpenStreetMap protected areas of Vietnam
description: Areas mapped as protected areas (boundary=protected_area, with protect_class) or nature reserves (leisure=nature_reserve) in Vietnam, with their outlines (for area and centre).

title: Di tích quốc gia đặc biệt (Việt Nam)
description: The list of special national relics (di tích quốc gia đặc biệt), by ranking round (each round is a decision of the Prime Minister), with location, category and coordinates; the linked articles give coordinates (GeoData) for the rest, or Wikidata (P625) when the article has none. Wikipedia compiles the list from the decisions and the Government portal; it is not itself an official register.

title: Statistical Yearbooks of Vietnam 2010-2018 (full editions)
publisher: National Statistics Office of Vietnam (NSO, formerly GSO)
license: No licence stated; official statistics, reused with attribution
description: Full yearbooks 2010 to 2018 (bilingual). Their by-province tables give the years 2010-2018 for the 63 provinces. Each year comes from the newest edition that prints it, and an edition is used only if it agrees with the newer editions on the years both print. Parsed by pipeline/nso/backfill.py into data/stats/series/; each row cites its edition and page.

title: Completed results of the 2019 Population and Housing Census
publisher: National Statistics Office of Vietnam (NSO, formerly GSO)
license: No licence stated; official statistics, reused with attribution
description: Kết quả toàn bộ Tổng điều tra dân số và nhà ở năm 2019 (census day 1 April 2019), Table 2: population by ethnic group (54 groups, plus foreigners and not stated) for the nation, the 6 regions and the 63 provinces of the time. Parsed by pipeline/nso/census2019.py into data/stats/census2019/; every province's groups add up to its total and every group's provinces add up to the national row.
used_for: Ethnic groups in the province panels

title: Wikipedia articles on Vietnam's capitals, dynasties and provinces
publisher: Wikipedia (English and Vietnamese), via the MediaWiki API
description: Plain-text extracts and coordinates of the articles cited by the timeline's history events (capitals from Phong Châu and Cổ Loa to Huế and Hà Nội, dynasties, the French conquest, 1945–1976, and the province splits and mergers up to the 34 provinces of 2025). Each event keeps the sentence that states its date; dates before about 1000 CE follow tradition and chronicles.

title: Wikipedia articles cited by the History list
publisher: Wikipedia (English and Vietnamese), via the MediaWiki API
description: Plain-text extracts, coordinates and revision ids of the articles cited by the History list (web/data/history.json): dynasties and capitals, the modern era, every change to the province map, railways, bridges, expressways, airports and ports, disasters, UNESCO heritage, economic integration, science and sport. Each event keeps the sentence of the article that states its date, and the revision it was checked against; dates before about 1000 CE follow tradition and chronicles.

title: Official notices cited by the History list
publisher: Government of Vietnam (xaydungchinhsach.chinhphu.vn); National Assembly newspaper (daibieunhandan.vn)
license: No licence stated; official news, quoted with attribution
description: Pages announcing National Assembly Standing Committee resolutions on new wards (2026), cited by History events whose details are not yet on Wikipedia. Each event keeps the page's sentence that states them.

title: Key results of the 2024 Intercensal Population and Housing Survey (1 April 2024)
publisher: National Statistics Office of Vietnam (NSO, formerly GSO)
license: No licence stated; official statistics, reused with attribution
description: Kết quả chủ yếu Điều tra dân số và nhà ở giữa kỳ thời điểm 0 giờ 01/4/2024 (a sample survey), Table 5 (printed p.121-122): sex ratio, dependency ratio, age structure and ageing index (people aged 60 and over per 100 under 15) for the nation, the 6 regions and the 63 provinces of the time.

title: DesInventar disaster loss database of Viet Nam
publisher: UNDRR DesInventar; records of Viet Nam's Central Committee for Flood and Storm Control (CCFSC)
license: No licence stated; shared publicly by the contributing government, reused with attribution
description: One record per event and province, 1989-2010 (plus one record of 2019): event type, date, deaths, missing, injured, houses destroyed. The 63 former provinces (Hà Tây, merged into Hà Nội in 2008, is added to Hà Nội).

title: SatPM2.5 V6.GL.03 annual surface PM2.5, Asia, 0.01°
publisher: Atmospheric Composition Analysis Group, Washington University in St. Louis (van Donkelaar, Martin et al.)
description: Annual mean ground-level fine particulate matter (PM2.5, µg/m³) for 2024 at 0.01° (~1.1 km), estimated from satellite aerosol optical depth, the GEOS-Chem model and ground monitors (Shen et al. 2024, ACS ES&T Air, doi:10.1021/acsestair.3c00054). Averaged per hex.

title: Statistical Yearbook of Vietnam 2025 (and 2024) and PX-Web database
publisher: National Statistics Office of Vietnam (NSO, formerly GSO)
license: No licence stated; official statistics, reused with attribution
description: Yearbook 2025, Part I (63 former provinces, 2025 preliminary): population, urban population, labour force, employment, unemployment, trained and informal labour, productivity, GRDP per person and growth, income, Gini, poverty, paddy rice, maize, cassava, sugarcane, tea, orange, retail sales, travel turnover, life expectancy, migration, internet use, IT skills, clean water, housing (2024). Its appendix (34 provinces of 2025): HDI, FDI, enterprises, doctors, forest cover, road deaths, pupils per teacher and the official 34-province rates. Yearbook 2024: area, literacy, HDI and FDI for the 63 former provinces (2024), university students (2023). PX-Web: population 2019–2025, enterprises 2024, employment by industry. Parsed into data/stats/ by pipeline/nso/; the appendix rice tables (Gia Lai and Khánh Hòa rows swapped) are replaced by sums of the former provinces.

title: Socio-economic situation reports, September and October 2026 (statistical tables)
license: No licence stated; official statistics, reused with attribution
description: Estimated GRDP growth for the first 9 months of 2026 (constant 2020 prices) and the index of industrial-enterprise employment at 1 October 2026, by the 34 provinces.

title: Provincial Competitiveness Index (PCI) 2022, 2024 and 2025
description: Survey-based business-climate score per province. 2022: VCCI's composite for all 63 former provinces; 2024: the composite for the top 30. PCI 2025 (34 provinces) publishes the nine sub-indices, their weights and rank groups but no composite score: the atlas computes it as 10 × the weighted mean of the sub-indices, weights from the PCI 2025 report (Figure A1.1 p.138, Table 4.2 p.105), and checks that it reproduces all 34 published rank groups (Table 4.3 p.107).
vintage: PCI 2025 (composite computed by the atlas; 2022 and 2024 in panels and the timeline)

title: Official exchange rate (PA.NUS.FCRF)
description: VND per USD, period average; every dong figure is converted at the 2024 rate (the 2025 rate is not yet published).
